references.text: Refers to the same service garments (bigde hasserad) and the holy garments for Aaron and his sons that were to be used in the sanctuary service.
Mentions the service garments for the work in the sanctuary, the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments for his sons for priestly service.
God gives instructions to make holy garments for Aaron for glory and beauty, including specific articles of clothing for priestly service.
Describes the garments that were to be made for Aaron's sons for priestly service so they could serve in the sanctuary.
Refers to the holy garments that were to pass from Aaron to his sons as a permanent ordinance for consecration and priestly service.
Describes how Moses clothed Aaron in the holy priestly garments during the consecration ceremony.
Mentions the use of the service garments (beged hasserad) in connection with service in the sanctuary.
Bridges the detailed description of the garments to the conclusion that they were made.
Concludes the narrative cycle concerning the making of the holy garments.
Expands the understanding of the meaning of the garments from their creation to an eternal succession for the priesthood.
Connects the making of the garments with their use in the anointing and ordination of priests.
Specifies how the tunics are included as part of the overall production of the priestly garments.
Shows the immediate use of the finished garments at the ordination of Aaron.
Highlights that although humans make the garments, it is God's holy act that makes the service valid.
